confirmed.suspectedCause: The F820 fix in this merge: the host scroll listener in src/content/index.ts now returns early when tabAt > userScrollAt, so no focus-driven scroll loads more on any list until the reader scrolls. Before, a focus scroll near the end loaded more, as F820's evidence shows for Up next (inferred for the other lists). Lead: limit the Tab exception to a list that has content after it in an open section (Up next before Comments), or end each loadable list with an explicit 'More' control (Block.more) that Tab reaches.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, medium, a regression from the F820 fix. Home in Sift: main focused, then 60 Tabs. The list stayed at 21 entries every 10 Tabs, and focus wrapped to the header ('Menu' at 30, 'Search' at 60). End then loaded 45. Watch page Comments opened with Enter, then 60 Tabs: 'sift 20 orig 20' throughout, and focus wrapped to Search twice. Original with Sift off: on home, Tab took the grid from 21 to 45 items by 100 Tabs. In comments, Tab took the threads from 20 to 40 by 150 Tabs. The cause is in the code: the host scroll listener in src/content/index.ts (around line 2520) has 'if (tabAt > userScrollAt) return;'. Tab sets tabAt (onSiftKey, line 894), and only wheel, touch, pointerdown or a scrolling key set userScrollAt. So after any Tab, a focus-driven scroll never loads more. Home and search have nothing after the list, so the F820 reason (reaching Comments after Up next) does not apply there. Inferred and not tested: a screen reader's browse-mode scrolling also loads nothing once the reader has pressed Tab.
confirmed.fix: In the host scroll listener in src/content/index.ts, keep the Tab exception only for a list that has more content after it in Sift's view (Up next before Comments, i.e. youtube.loadMore would pick Up next). Otherwise let a focus scroll near the end load more as before. Or end each loadable list with a focusable 'More' control (Block.more) that Tab reaches and that calls loadMore.

The content script did change (MARK_B), so a run mixes a new content script with an old service worker. Uninstall + install (the chrome.sh reload path) ran the new code (MARK_D). The tester's fix lead does not work. With the manifest version bumped to 9.9.9.1, .2 and .3, Chrome reported the new version from getManifest(), but the service worker was still MARK_A (n0c.ts). Deleting <profile>/Default/Service Worker/ScriptCache made the next launch fail to start the service worker. The launch after that ran the new code, and IndexedDB was kept. Or have chrome.sh start always end with a reload and print the running service worker's PROMPT_VERSION. Do not rely on a manifest version bump: tested, it does not refresh the service worker.
